message.reasoning: I'll write JUnit 4 tests targeting the Parser's public API (parse, parseBodyFragment), since that's how I can exercise the private method branches indirectly—covering comment parsing, CDATA, XML declarations, end tags, start tags, and text nodes. Continuing through the branch inventory, I need tests covering attribute parsing (quoted/unquoted values, missing equals), child-to-parent attachment rules (valid ancestors, body tag handling, empty elements), stack validity checks, and the various stack-popping logic for closing tags and finding suitable containers. Since Parser's internals are private, I'll exercise them indirectly through the public `parse(html, baseUri)` and `parseBodyFragment(bodyHtml, baseUri)` methods, inspecting the resulting Document tree. I'm planning test cases: basic tag/attribute/text parsing, well-formed and malformed comments, CDATA sections, XML declarations and DOCTYPE handling, empty end tags like ``, and malformed start tags where the tag name consumption yields an empty string. I also want to cover self-closing and void elements, raw-text elements like script/title/textarea, base tag resolution, the various attribute quoting styles, malformed attributes with no key, unclosed tags that trigger stack-popping logic, and implicit parent creation when elements appear outside valid ancestors (like a `` without a table), plus the edge case of the html tag sitting alone on the stack. With that outline I'm sketching concrete tests: parsing nested elements to check title and body text extraction, and parsing comments -- including tricky malformed comment syntax that exercises the chompTo("->") logic and whether the trailing dash gets stripped correctly.
